coverage_review.coverage: Both implicit TLS and STARTTLS: stalled-handshake cancellation plus provider retry; operation deadline closure; trusted login/mailbox round-trip; default-trust rejection before credentials; hostname rejection before credentials. Additional manual plain-socket upgrade rejection, manually attached existing SecureSocket round-trip, deterministic partial-write/readiness/flush-close order, and blocked-write abort.

Both modes and cancellation/deadline paths: real ClientHello observation, physical peer closure before test teardown without releasing the handshake, two attempts through the same provider, distinct sockets, and no plaintext LOGIN/AUTHENTICATE or credential bytes.

Both modes: isolated trusted CA, 1 MiB payload with delayed server reads and exact SHA-256, subsequent capability reply, default-trust rejection of the same certificate. Additional abort of an open idle addStream producer must reject and cancel that producer.

review_findings.finding: Incoming Mail test fixtures require ClientConnection factory APIs while incoming Zotero capturing test used Socket APIs. Final source uses the Mail adapter and type-only round-trip capture patch, retaining all assertions.

Updated process-reaping race control catches FileNotFoundError/ProcessLookupError between observation and read while retaining bounded termination checks. Fresh complete core/store gate is required for the new model hash assertion and changed control input; prior receipts are preserved separately.

Delayed 1 MiB real TLS writes prove exact payload and usable replies but do not by themselves guarantee operating-system partial writes. The independent fake RawSocket test forces 3-byte writes and readiness ordering.

All TLS certificate trust uses isolated test contexts, fixed intentionally public fixture keys, and local loopback endpoints. Passing these tests does not establish live-account, external-server, vault/OAuth, installed Studio/OS IME, actual browser offline lifecycle, or linguistic acceptance.
